messages:
anya: Flagging a customer case where a streaming truncation + route failover resulted in two tool-call token charges. Minimal repro attached.
kevin: Curious if this is the same pattern as before (retry creates new ephemeral session) or something different. Any routing hops in the trace?
dina: Trace shows: client->edge (us-west)->router (swapped to gpu-8bit in us-east) -> session reset. After reset we replay the last turn and the toolcall fires again.
anya: Log snippet: ```[2026-03-22T23:05:10Z] stream: eof at seq=1024; wrote toolcall id=tlc-77; [2026-03-22T23:05:11Z] route: model swap -> clearing ephemeral headers; [2026-03-22T23:05:11Z] reconnect: client replay -> toolcall id=tlc-77-R1```
kevin: Hmm. Two options: force client to carry idempotency_token/session_id on retry (preferred), or implement server-side idempotency fingerprinting.
anya: We can't rely on all clients adding session_id. We should have a fallback. Suggestion: create an `idemp_fingerprint` computed as sha256(tool_name + normalized_payload + approx_timestamp_bucket) and use that to dedupe provisional charges within a short TTL.
dina: I like fingerprinting but worry about collisions and legitimate parallel calls with same payload. Maybe require three conditions: same fingerprint, same origin_customer_id, and previous event state is PROVISIONAL (not CONFIRMED). Only then suppress second provisional.
kevin: Good safeguard. Also keep raw events immutable: mark a derived "suppression_record" instead of deleting the second event. That preserves replayability for billing reconciliation.
ops-bot: Note: add feature-flag "idemp_fingerprint_dedupe" and per-customer opt-out tag `no_server_dedupe`.
console-team: For console UX, ops want to be able to filter by "suppressed by dedupe" and view the original raw events. Also show when fingerprint matched and the dedupe rule used.
anya: Telemetry plan: emit `dedupe.fingerprint` and `dedupe.reason` and a boolean `dedupe.suppressed`. Keep an audit log table with both original and suppressed events linked by `dedupe.trace_id`.
dina: We'll need unit + integration tests that simulate fast reconnects and swaps. Canary rollout: start in non-critical region and measure suppressed_count vs confirmed_delta.
kevin: Alerting: trigger if suppression rate > 0.5% of retries or if confirmed_charge_delta increases after enabling dedupe.
anya: Edgecase: what about toolcalls that have side-effects on downstream systems (e.g., DB writes)? If we suppress server-side, we must ensure the toolcall wasn't actually executed on the model/service. How do we guarantee safety?
dina: We can only dedupe provisional charges, not dedupe the actual tool execution. If the retry actually made the downstream call, we'll still have two executions but we only suppress the provisional billing event until ledger reconciliation. That means ops might still see double-execution in logs—need to be explicit in docs.
kevin: So suppression affects only billing events, not control flow. If customers want server-side prevention of duplicate executions they need to enable idempotency in their tool implementations. We'll document that.
anya: Add console copy: "Suppressed provisional charge — potential duplicate due to streaming retry. Click to view raw events and trace." Include an action: "Request replay audit" which creates a ticket for billing ops.
ops-bot: Draft ticket RW-8991 created: "idemp-fingerprint dedupe for retry-induced toolcall provisional charges". Labels: billing, eng-platform, telemetry, console.
dina: I'll pick up the server patch, tests, and canary. ETA 2w.
kevin: I'll own telemetry & alerting. ETA 5 days for dashboards.
console-team: We'll do prototype UI and copy next sprint.
anya: Reminder: add a toggle in the control plane to annotate suppressed events rather than hiding them for first-phase rollout.
dina: Will do. Also plan a small migration to backfill fingerprint fields for recent events to validate heuristics before enabling suppression.
kevin: Sounds like a plan. We'll reconvene if backfill shows unexpected collision rate.
anya: Thanks all, ping RW-8991 for updates.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-03-27 14:00 UTC (5% traffic) — monitoring hooks added.
